findings.what: The Go back script goes back only when `ours && history.length > 1`. The spec's decision says history goes back whenever document.referrer is same-origin, and it rejected `history.length > 1`. The extra guard is a condition the decision doesn't state. The AC-8 test regex doesn't pin it either way.
findings.fix: Remove `&& history.length > 1` so the condition is only the same-origin referrer, or record the owner's call in the spec.

findings.what: The state-table row '/, no items' is tested only for the 'No items yet.' text (existing test). It doesn't check that the list is hidden, that the filter links are shown with All current, or that Go back is absent. No test checks that Go back is hidden on the 200 rows. Row 4 (known category, no items) checks the links but not Go back.
findings.fix: In the empty-table test, assert that there is no <li>, that currentLinks is ['All'], and that 'Go back' is absent. Add the same 'Go back' absence check to the AC-5 and AC-6 tests.

lenses.note: The change follows the spec's intent, apart from the findings.
One departure from a decision: the extra history.length guard in Go back. The 'go' commit only recorded the owner's acceptance and changed no acceptance item.
Tests name each AC and would fail against broken code. The state-table coverage has gaps (see the finding). I did not run the suite, because CI runs it.
README is updated and matches the behaviour.
Queries are parameterised, encoding and escaping are correct, and no other defects found.
Output is HTML-escaped, SQL is bound, and the inline script uses no user input. No planted instructions found.
